newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq resumes downward slide in late selling.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq resumes downward slide in late selling.

text.p: Nasdaq shares slipped on Friday, as technology stocks failed to hold on to moderate gains seen on Thursday.
The Nasdaq composite index shed 5.19 points or 0.41 percent to close unofficially at 1254.07. The Dow industrials also ended slightly lower.

"There was a bit of a spike in techs on Thursday, but no followthrough today. The market is nervous about what Greenspan will do next week, so there could be some selling into Monday as well," said Nelson Gold, senior vice president of over-the-counter trading at Interstate-Johnson Lane Corp.
Investors have been increasingly skittish, selling off before next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, traders said.

Several large capitalization technology stocks lost ground Friday, with Intel Corp losing 2-3/4 to 130-1/2 and Microsoft Corp slipping 2 to 94. Dismal quarterly forecasts rocked several companies, with Outback Steakhouse Inc falling 4-1/2 to 19-1/8 and GeoWorks Inc dropping 4-3/4 to 7-1/4.
Overall, losing issues beat gainers 2130 to 2007 on total volume of about 582 million shares.
